title: Noun sentence - abnormally normal order of components
description: Sentences with Muta'allaq bil khabar muqaddam + Mubtada muakkhar: which become "X has ..." (لِ, عِنْدَ), which become "There is ..." (فِي, بَيْنَ), and when the translation needs ONLY. Every example is a Quranic noun sentence with its reference.
source: Owner's lesson notes: Lesson 5, When abnormal sequence becomes normal (possession and existence)

questions.text: When the Mubtada muakkhar is a common word (with tanween), what does the order MBK (muqaddam) + M (muakkhar) mean?

options.text: It always adds exclusivity, so ONLY is added
It is the normal way to say "X has ..." or "There is ...", so no ONLY is added
It is a mistake; the Mubtada must come first
It turns the sentence into a question

questions.explanation: With a common Mubtada, this order is simply how Arabic says that someone has something or that something exists somewhere. The abnormal order has become normal, so it adds no ONLY.

questions.text: Which two words at the start of the MBK give the "X has ..." pattern?

options.text: لِ (harf of jar) and عِنْدَ (special mudhaaf)
فِي (harf of jar) and بَيْنَ (special mudhaaf)
لِ (harf of jar) and بَيْنَ (special mudhaaf)
فِي (harf of jar) and عِنْدَ (special mudhaaf)

questions.explanation: MBK with لِ + M = X has ..., and MBK with the special mudhaaf عِنْدَ + M = X has ...

questions.text: Which two words at the start of the MBK give the "There is ..." pattern?

options.text: لِ (harf of jar) and عِنْدَ (special mudhaaf)
فِي (harf of jar) and بَيْنَ (special mudhaaf)
عِنْدَ (special mudhaaf) and بَيْنَ (special mudhaaf)
لِ (harf of jar) and فِي (harf of jar)

questions.explanation: MBK with فِي + M = there is ..., and MBK with the special mudhaaf بَيْنَ + M = there is ... These sentences say that something exists in a certain place.

questions.text: In a sentence with MBK (muqaddam) + M (muakkhar), when do we add ONLY to the translation?

options.text: When the Mubtada muakkhar is common (it has tanween)
Whenever the MBK starts with فِي
Never; this order never adds ONLY
When the Mubtada muakkhar is proper (it has ال, or it is an إِضَافَة such as دِينُكُمْ)

questions.explanation: A proper Mubtada did not have to move back, so moving the MBK forward adds exclusivity and ONLY goes before the muqaddam part. A common Mubtada has to come after, so the order is normal and has no ONLY.

questions.text: Which translation fits وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (Al-Baqarah 2:10)?

options.text: And ONLY they have a painful punishment.
And there is a painful punishment between them.
And they have a painful punishment.
And their punishment is ONLY painful.

questions.explanation: لَهُمْ (لِ + owner) is the MBK muqaddam and عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ is the Mubtada muakkhar. لِ gives "X has", and عَذَابٌ is common (tanween), so there is no ONLY.

questions.text: Which translation fits فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ (Al-Baqarah 2:10)?

options.text: In their hearts there is a disease.
They have ONLY a disease in their hearts.
Their hearts have the disease.
ONLY in their hearts is the disease.

questions.explanation: فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ is the MBK muqaddam and مَرَضٌ is the Mubtada muakkhar. فِي gives "There is", and مَرَضٌ is common (tanween), so there is no ONLY.

questions.text: Which translation fits وَعِنْدَنَا كِتَابٌ حَفِيظٌ (Qaf 50:4)?

options.text: And ONLY We have the preserving record.
And there is a record between Us.
And We have a preserving record.
And Our record is ONLY preserving.

questions.explanation: عِنْدَنَا (the special mudhaaf عِنْدَ + owner) gives "X has". كِتَابٌ حَفِيظٌ is common (tanween), so the order is normal and there is no ONLY.

questions.text: Which translation fits وَبَيْنَهُمَا حِجَابٌ (Al-Araf 7:46)?

options.text: And the two of them have a barrier.
And ONLY between the two of them is the barrier.
And between the two of them there is a barrier.
And their barrier is between them.

questions.explanation: بَيْنَهُمَا (the special mudhaaf بَيْنَ) is the MBK muqaddam and gives "There is". حِجَابٌ is common (tanween), so there is no ONLY.

questions.text: Which translation fits لَهُ الْمُلْكُ (At-Taghabun 64:1)?

options.text: He has a kingdom.
There is a kingdom for Him.
The kingdom ONLY has Him.
ONLY He has the kingdom.

questions.explanation: لَهُ (لِ + owner) gives "X has". الْمُلْكُ is proper (it has ال), so moving لَهُ forward adds exclusivity, and ONLY goes before the muqaddam part: "ONLY He has the kingdom".

questions.text: Which translation fits وَعِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ (Az-Zukhruf 43:85)?

options.text: And He has a knowledge of an hour.
And ONLY He has the knowledge of the Hour.
And there is the knowledge of the Hour between them.
And the knowledge of the Hour has ONLY Him.

questions.explanation: عِنْدَهُ gives "X has". عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ is an إِضَافَة ending in a proper word, so it is proper and the translation needs ONLY before the muqaddam part.

questions.text: Which pattern fits فِيهَا عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ (Al-Ghashiyah 88:12)?

options.text: "There is ..." with no ONLY: In it there is a flowing spring.
"X has ..." with no ONLY: It has a flowing spring.
"There is ..." with ONLY: ONLY in it is a flowing spring.
"X has ..." with ONLY: ONLY it has the flowing spring.

questions.explanation: فِيهَا starts with فِي, which gives "There is". عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ is common (tanween), so there is no ONLY.

questions.text: Which pattern fits وَعَلَىٰ أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةٌ (Al-Baqarah 2:7)?

options.text: "X has ..." with no ONLY: Their eyes have the covering.
"There is ..." with no ONLY: Over their eyes there is a covering.
"There is ..." with ONLY: ONLY over their eyes is the covering.
"X has ..." with ONLY: ONLY they have a covering.

questions.explanation: عَلَىٰ أَبْصَارِهِمْ tells us where the covering is, so this is a sentence of existence: "There is". غِشَاوَةٌ is common (tanween), so there is no ONLY.

questions.text: Which translation fits وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ (Yusuf 12:76)?

options.text: And every possessor of knowledge has one more knowing.
And above every possessor of knowledge there is one more knowing.
And ONLY above every possessor of knowledge is the All-Knowing.
And the one more knowing is above ONLY some people of knowledge.

questions.explanation: فَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ is a place word with its chain, the MBK muqaddam, so it says where something exists: "There is". عَلِيمٌ is common (tanween), so there is no ONLY.

questions.text: Which of these needs ONLY in its translation?

options.text: وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ (Al-Baqarah 2:7)
فِيهَا سُرُرٌ مَرْفُوعَةٌ (Al-Ghashiyah 88:13)
وَعِنْدَهُ أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ (Ar-Rad 13:39)
بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ (Ar-Rahman 55:20)

questions.explanation: أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ is an إِضَافَة ending in a proper word, so it is proper: "And ONLY He has the Mother of the Book". In the others the Mubtada (عَذَابٌ, سُرُرٌ, بَرْزَخٌ) is common, so no ONLY.

questions.text: Which of these does not need ONLY in its translation?

options.text: لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ (Al-Kafirun 109:6)
فَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ (Al-Jathiyah 45:36)
وَعِنْدَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ (Al-Anam 6:59)
فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ (At-Tin 95:6)

questions.explanation: أَجْرٌ is common (tanween), so the order is normal: "They have a reward never cut off". The other Mubtadas (دِينُكُمْ, الْحَمْدُ, مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ) are proper, so they take ONLY.

questions.text: Which translation fits لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِيَ دِينِ (Al-Kafirun 109:6)?

options.text: You have a religion, and I have a religion.
There is your religion for you, and there is my religion for me.
ONLY you have your religion, and ONLY I have my religion.
Your religion has ONLY you, and my religion has ONLY me.

questions.explanation: Each half is لِ + owner (X has) before a Mubtada joined to a pronoun (دِينُكُمْ, دِينِ), which makes it proper. So both halves need ONLY before the owner.

questions.text: In بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ (Ar-Rahman 55:20), which part is the Mubtada muakkhar?

options.text: بَرْزَخٌ
بَيْنَهُمَا
بَيْنَ
هُمَا

questions.explanation: بَيْنَهُمَا (the special mudhaaf بَيْنَ with its mudhaaf ilaih) is the MBK muqaddam, and بَرْزَخٌ is the Mubtada muakkhar: "Between the two of them there is a barrier".

questions.text: Why is there no ONLY in the translation of فِيهِمَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ (Ar-Rahman 55:68)?

options.text: Because فِيهِمَا is the Mubtada
Because the sentence has a Khabar after the Mubtada
Because فِي can never take ONLY
Because the Mubtada فَاكِهَةٌ is common (tanween), so the order is normal

questions.explanation: فِيهِمَا is the MBK muqaddam and فَاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ is the Mubtada muakkhar. It is common, so the order is normal: "In both of them there is fruit, date palms and pomegranates".

questions.text: In وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ (Al-Baqarah 2:7), which part is the Muta'allaq bil khabar muqaddam?

options.text: عَذَابٌ
عَظِيمٌ
عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
لَهُمْ

questions.explanation: لَهُمْ is a Jaar Majroor (لِ + هُمْ), the MBK muqaddam. عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ is the Mubtada muakkhar: "And they have a great punishment".

questions.text: Which pairing of ayah and pattern is right?

options.text: وَعِنْدَنَا كِتَابٌ حَفِيظٌ (50:4): "X has"; فِيهَا عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ (88:12): "There is"
وَعِنْدَنَا كِتَابٌ حَفِيظٌ (50:4): "There is"; فِيهَا عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ (88:12): "X has"
وَبَيْنَهُمَا حِجَابٌ (7:46): "X has"; وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (2:10): "There is"
وَبَيْنَهُمَا حِجَابٌ (7:46): "X has"; وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (2:10): "X has"

questions.explanation: عِنْدَ and لِ give "X has"; فِي and بَيْنَ give "There is". So 50:4 and 2:10 are "X has", and 88:12 and 7:46 are "There is".
